lines.trans: Ah, I get it, are you ashamed of me?
Must we meet so that nobody sees us?
No, you are the most beautiful girl in the world.
I simply lied to my mom that I was at work.
You will see for yourself right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это замечательно, ты будешь первым поваром России.
examples.trans: That is wonderful, you will be the first chef in Russia.
And you wrote a culinary book.

examples.text: Рассчитали, от трех до пяти тысяч за блюдо.
examples.trans: We calculated them, from three to five thousand per dish.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('alive').

examples.trans: Do not worry, Lyova.

examples.text: Я же не знаю, как у вас принято за девушками ухаживать.
examples.trans: I do not know how it is customary in your country to court girls.
Lyova, are you alive?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.
It was an interesting movie, right?
Well yes, bye.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'екунда'). Common feminine noun meaning 'second' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Yes, wait a second.
One second. I'll call right now.
Wait one second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'almost, nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She almost spotted me.
I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

examples.text: Не знаю, я на экран не смотрел особо.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not really look at the screen.
They offered me a new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to notice, spot', paired with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: She almost spotted me.
Who almost spotted you?
He did not notice the loss.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.
Vitya, I am a fish.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, а цены вы уже рассчитали?
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, have you already calculated the prices?
This is a dish by Viktor Barinov!
Not Vitya, but Viktor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mom' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай за мою маму и за ее мудрые советы.
examples.trans: Let's drink to my mom and her wise advice.
Yes, Mom, I am not at home.
Alright, bye, Mom.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vitya, this is my restaurant!
This is my restaurant!

examples.text: Это мой ресторан, и я решаю, что здесь едят.
examples.trans: This is my restaurant, and I decide what people eat here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.
Otherwise I will die before my time.
Vitya, I am a fish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, я ничего не понял.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not understand anything.

examples.text: Он сказал, что половину слов в меню не понял.
examples.trans: He said that he did not understand half the words on the menu.

examples.text: Я не понял, она у нас работает?
examples.trans: I do not understand, does she work here with us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тесняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'are ashamed / shy of'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и стесняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and are ashamed on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют стесняться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to are ashamed.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are changing the restaurant's concept.

examples.text: Может, мы пока старое меню оставим?
examples.trans: Maybe we should keep the old menu for now?

examples.text: Вы еще меня благодарить будете, когда мы звезду получим.
examples.trans: You will thank me yet when we get the star.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

examples.text: Мы должны встречаться так, чтобы никто не видел?
examples.trans: Must we meet so that nobody sees us?

examples.text: И он отстраняет вас от должности.
examples.trans: And he is removing you from office.
I have to work.

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to date / meet', paired with 'встретиться'.

examples.text: Мы должны встречаться так, чтобы никто не видел?
examples.trans: Must we meet so that nobody sees us?
We've been dating for a month.
We meet often.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Итак, в новом меню морские гребешки.
examples.trans: So, on the new menu are sea scallops.

examples.text: А также гусиная грудка в соусе.
examples.trans: And also goose breast in sauce.

examples.text: Шеф, а почему блюда такие маленькие?
examples.trans: Chef, why are the dishes so tiny?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is the occasion?
What does that mean?

examples.text: Прости, что-то я удержаться не смог.
examples.trans: Sorry, somehow I could not hold back.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A man's best ally is alcohol.
Nikolai Maryanovich, my respects!
No problem at all, Vitya.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Мы должны встречаться так, чтобы никто не видел?
examples.trans: Must we meet so that nobody sees us?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нет старого меню, есть только новое меню.
examples.trans: There is no old menu, there is only the new menu.
No, I have not kissed her yet.
No, I will not drink to that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('most').

examples.trans: Decide for yourself.

examples.text: Давай выпьем за наших девушек, они у нас самые лучшие.
examples.trans: Let's drink to our girls, they are the very best.

examples.text: Мы вот овощи отобрали самые красивые.

examples.trans: We selected the most beautiful vegetables here.

examples.text: Нет, ты самая красивая девушка на свете.
examples.trans: No, you are the most beautiful girl in the world.
Look how beautiful you've become!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не знаю, я на экран не смотрел особо.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not really look at the screen.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'world' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Слушай, Света, ты же знаешь, что ты нравишься одному человеку?

examples.text: Нет, ты самая красивая девушка на свете.

examples.text: Ты мне сам вчера говорил, что Света твоя девушка.
examples.trans: You told me yourself yesterday that Sveta was your girlfriend.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Sorry, a new job?

examples.text: У вас сначала у родителей разрешение просить надо.
examples.trans: In your country you first have to ask the parents for permission.

examples.text: Прости, что-то я удержаться не смог.
examples.trans: Sorry, somehow I could not hold back.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'врать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lied'.

examples.text: Я просто маме наврал, что я на работе.
examples.trans: I simply lied to my mom that I was at work.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наврать вовремя.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are doing', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: I did not tell you, I wanted to make a surprise.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'целовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kiss', paired with 'целовать'.

examples.trans: Well, did you kiss Gulya?

examples.text: Знаешь, как мы с Настей поцеловались первый раз?
examples.trans: Do you know how Nastya and I kissed for the first time?
I want to kiss you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Сейчас собираюсь вводить новое авторское меню.
examples.trans: Right now I am going to introduce a new auteur menu.
We will prepare everything right now!

examples.trans: You'll see!
I saw Dad.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!
